chunks: It is narrated from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Dirhams for dirhams, when one of the two contains lead, while being equal weight for equal weight.
He said: Repeat it. So I repeated it to him. Then he said: Repeat it. So I repeated it to him.
Then he said: “I see no harm in it.”

key_terms.أَعِدْ: repeat; the Imam’s instruction to restate the question
key_terms.بَأْسًا: harm or objection; meaning legal impropriety is not seen in it
key_terms.رَصَاصٌ: lead; an admixture present in one of the coins
key_terms.وَزْنًا بِوَزْنٍ: equal in weight; the condition mentioned for the exchange

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to exchange dirhams for dirhams if one of them contains lead but both are equal in weight?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on exchanging dirhams for dirhams when one coin contains lead but both are equal in weight. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام ultimately states that he sees no harm in such an exchange, indicating its permissibility in this form.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4042 - It is narrated from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about exchanging dirhams for dirhams, where one of them contains lead, but they are equal in weight.

Imam (as) said: "Repeat the question."
So I repeated it to him.
Then Imam (as) said: "Repeat it again."
I repeated it again,
and Imam (as) said: "I see no harm in it."
